newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India selling pressure still there.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India selling pressure still there.

text.p: Selling pressure in the Indian global depositary receipt (GDR) market continued on Tuesday, albeit at a slower pace, but, with Bombay hanging by a thread, traders expect renewed falls.
"The undertone is very weak, the year low will be tested sooner rather than later," a broker said.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 0.11 points at 58.59 points, with the premium over the local market at 9.35 percent after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 24.49 points to 3,027.35.
Some analysts believe that the BSE-30 share index could go as low as 2,400 before it rebounds and the Indian GDRs are already down more than a quarter since the start of the year.
Political worries over the future of India's coalition government and slowing industrial growth have combined to hit the share index.
"This market will only turn when there is the perception of compelling value combined with liquidity and confidence in the local investors. When that is, I do not know," said the broker.
Among individual stocks, State Bank of India is now below its offer price of last week at $13.75/$14.25 after being issued at $14.25.
"I thought the stock would come down in the aftermarket. It looks as though I was right. There will be plenty of opportunity to get in later," said a trader.
Elsewhere, the Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 0.30 points at 69.23, a premium of 27.34 percent over the local market, after the Korea Composite Index rose 2.29 points to 797.62.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.28 points, at 90.77, a premium of 2.29 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index fell 35.51 points or 0.54 percent to 6,584.91.
